title: Platform developer experience: signal curation and on-call playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Summary:

This playbook documents the platform-level approach for curating telemetry signals that matter to developer experience (DX), defining actionable alerts, and prescribing on-call runbook steps to resolve or mitigate DX incidents. It codifies what to monitor, how to translate noisy telemetry into operator action, and how to close the loop with product/engineers to reduce future signal noise.

Scope:
- Applies to all platform services that directly affect developer-facing operations: API gateway, token billing pipeline, model routing service, prefix/KV cache, and console (UI) endpoints.
- Does NOT cover deep model quality regressions (handled by applied-ml-and-evals) or infra security incidents (security-and-compliance).

When to use this document:
1) When adding or modifying alerts that influence developer SLA or onboarding flows.
2) During on-call incidents where developer-facing metrics show degradation (console errors, onboarding failures, account provisioning, token attribution mismatches).
3) For quarterly signal hygiene reviews and alert burn-rate pruning.

Signal taxonomy (how we think about telemetry):
- User-facing errors: 5xx/4xx surfacing in console/API for authenticated users.
- Provisioning & billing: failed reservations, billing reconciliation errors, token attribution gaps.
- Latency & availability: p50/p95/p99 for API surface and console UI requests.
- Cost anomalies: per-tenant token-rate spikes or sudden embedding surges.
- Operational anomalies: KV prefix cache miss storm, hot-shard eviction, model-swap rollback.

Priority mapping:
- P0: System-wide developer outage preventing any onboarding or API auth (SLO burn > 5%/hr).
- P1: Significant subset of customers (>1% active tenants or one tier-A customer) seeing degraded performance or incorrect billing.
- P2: Localized errors or performance regressions with limited impact.
- P3: Cosmetic UI regressions, telemetry gaps, or non-blocking clogs.

Concrete SLOs and thresholds (platform-level defaults):
| Metric | Target | Alert threshold | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| API request success rate (prod, tokenized requests) | 99.95% rolling 1h | <99.5% rolling 15m | Escalate P0 if sustained >15m |
| API p95 latency (gen endpoints) | <250ms | >400ms sustained 10m | Use region shard breakdown |
| Console page load (first-contentful-paint) | <600ms | >1200ms 10m | Measure synthetic + real-user metrics |
| Token-attribution reconciliation error rate | <0.01% | >0.1% 30m | Correlate with billing pipeline logs |
| KV prefix-cache miss-rate | <2% | >8% 5m | Prefetch candidate or rehydrate step required |

Alert design principles:
- Alerts must map to an operator action or an automatic remediation. If there is no clear action, the signal should be surfaced as an observation-only dashboard.
- Group low-level signals into fused alerts (e.g., token-billing-pipeline-failure) to avoid pager storms.
- Add a ‘developer-impact’ tag to alerts that indicate customer-visible regressions.
- Each alert must declare owner, escalation path, and runbook link.

Example alert (Prometheus/Alertmanager):
- alert: DeveloperAPI_High_P95_Latency
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="developer-api"}[5m])) by (le, route)) > 0.4
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
    impact: developer-experience
  annotations:
    runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/developer-api-latency-mitigation
    owners: eng-platform-api

Runbook: Developer API high p95 latency (owner: eng-platform-api)
1) Triage:
   a) Check global dashboard and identify affected routes and regions.
   b) Run: curl -s "https://obs-redwood.internal/api/v1/instances?service=developer-api" | jq .status
   c) Confirm whether the issue is server-side (inference runtime backpressure) or client-side (large batches).
2) Immediate mitigations (choose one based on cause):
   - If KV prefix cache miss storm: trigger cache rehydrate job: /ops/scripts/rehydrate-prefix-cache --scope region=<region> --shard=<shard-id>. Notify cache-ops channel.
   - If model routing backlog: enable temporary routing-fallback to smaller-quantized variant: /infra/rollout-model-variant --id <variant> --reason "latency mitigation".
   - If autoscaler lag: run manual scale: /kubectl scale deployment developer-api --replicas=<n> --namespace=prod
3) Communication:
   - Post initial incident summary in #platform-incident with severity and preliminary cause.
   - If customers affected, update incident page and service status page per comms template.
4) Postmortem checklist (owner: incident lead):
   - Create postmortem within 72 hours.
   - Add concrete corrective actions (signal deduplication, prefetch tuning, autoscaler tuning).

On-call playbook for developer-impact alerts:
- Pager assignment: default two-person rotation drawn from eng-platform oncall roster. Primary handles triage and mitigation; secondary coordinates cross-team escalations.
- Escalation policy: after 15 minutes unresolved, escalate to Platform SRE lead; after 60 minutes unresolved and P0, page senior infra oncall.
- Customer comms cadence: 30m initial notice, hourly updates until mitigation, final summary sent in 24h.

Signal hygiene process (quarterly):
1) Gather list of alerts that paged in the quarter with burn counts.
2) Categorize each alert: actionable (kept), observation->dashboard (converted), noisy->tuned, redundant->merged.
3) Owners must submit tuning or deprecation PRs within two weeks of categorization.
4) Track progress in a quarterly scoreboard: target 40% reduction in noisy pages year-over-year.

Dashboards & queries (developer-facing examples):
- Developer experience overview dashboard (owner: eng-platform-observability): p50/p95/p99, failed onboarding flows, token reconciliation status, top-ten tenants by error rate.
- PromQL snippets:
  - 5xx rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="console",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)
  - Token spike detection: sum by (tenant_id)(increase(token_events_total[10m])) / avg_over_time(active_tenant_connections[1h]) > 4.0

Roadmap items (next 12 months):
- Q4 2025: Implement fused developer-impact alerting layer (event fusion service) to reduce redundant pages by 50%. Owner: eng-platform/observability.
- Q1 2026: Add ability to attach operator quick-actions to alerts (rehydrate cache, rollback model variant) from the alert UI. Owner: eng-platform/console.
- Q2 2026: Automate signal housekeeping (auto-snooze repeat alerts with known mitigations) and produce a monthly noise report.

Retrospective example (sample action items from a recent DX incident):
- Root cause: aggressive cache eviction policy during noisy onboarding experiment.
- Short-term fixes: revert eviction policy and add extra cache warmers.
- Long-term: add synthetic onboarding traffic to preheat cache and a gating experiment flag.
- Owners assigned: cache-team (short-term), onboarding-product (long-term).

Appendix A — Ownership & Escalation contacts:
- eng-platform-observability: obs-owner@redwood.com
- eng-platform-api: api-owner@redwood.com
- platform-sre-lead: sre-lead@redwood.com

Appendix B — Playbook maintenance policy:
- This document is reviewed at least once per quarter by eng-platform Observability.
- All runbook changes must be made via PR in the runbook repo and linked here.
